correctness.rationale: Proof constructs the unique invariant stochastic convolution, conditions on Poisson history to obtain a Gaussian mixture, exactly factors the variance deficit into an independent beta-power variable times a uniformly positive random factor, and integrates the resulting exact endpoint density by a justified Laplace scaling. The constant is expressed as an absolutely convergent stationary-moment series. Conditional normal moment formula gives a sharp reset-rate threshold at eta=kappa/(2D). Analytically all parameters are within the theorem domain. The independent exact-arithmetic checker compares two moment recursions and generator moments over five parameter sets.

originality.rationale: Galla 2026 gives a second-order approximate stationary law and no exact fixed-s reset stationary Gaussian tail or exponential-moment threshold; Kolb–Wübker treats primarily driftless Brownian partial resetting and mentions OU only in a Doob-transform example. The 2022/2024 driftless results instead have exponential spatial tails. Direct mathematical-record and published-primary searches uncovered no theorem stating the exact OU variance endpoint coefficient, the Gaussian-with-polynomial density/tail constant, and the reset-rate critical moment transition together. Classical mixture endpoint methods remain a potentially dominating general theorem: the conclusion is qualified pending independent priority review.
residual_risks: Broad endpoint-Laplace theorems for Gaussian variance mixtures may subsume the method and model as a special case.
Some exact partial-resetting papers were compared through abstracts only; their complete supplementary material was not fully inspected.
No independent verification or historical priority review has been performed.

value.rationale: The exact far-tail equivalence and prefactor quantify rare reset-free fluctuation events in a model explicitly motivated by new diffusion-approximation work. They establish a nontrivial invariant (a finite-endpoint variance power law with computable constant) and a sharp reset-rate critical moment boundary. The contrast with the approximate polynomial tail isolates a natural failure of a frequent-small-reset approximation for rare events, without disputing bulk accuracy. This is a motivated structural boundary rather than a routine substitution or numerical improvement.
